questions.question: Three articles are bought at Rs.180 each. One of them is sold at a loss of 10%. If the other two articles are sold so as to gain 25% on the whole transaction, then what is the gain percentage on the two articles?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of three articles = Rs. 180 each

Loss = 10%

Gain = 25% 

**Formula used:**

Gain = SP – CP

Gain% = Gain/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

CP of three articles = Rs. (180 × 3) = Rs. 540

Total gain% on whole transaction = 25%

So, 

SP of the three articles = Rs. (540 × 125/100)

⇒ Rs. 675

SP of the first article = Rs. (180 × 90)/100 

⇒ Rs. 162

CP of the other two articles = Rs. (180 × 2) = Rs. 360

SP of the other two articles = Rs. (675 – 162) = Rs. 513

Gain on two articles =Rs. (513 – 360) = Rs. 153

Gain% on the two articles = (153/360 × 100)

⇒ (15,300/360)

⇒ 42.5%

**∴ The required gain% on the two articles is 42.5%**

questions.question: The mean of 100 items is 47. It was discovered that three items which should have been 60,70, 80 were wrongly read as 40, 20, 50, respectively. The correct mean is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The mean of 100 items = 47

Items added = 60, 70, 80

Items wrongly replaced = 40, 20, 50

**Formula used:**

Average = sum of observations/Number of observations

**Calculation:**

According to the question

The mean of 100 items = (100 × 47) = 4700

Sum of items added = (60 + 70 + 80) = 210

Sum of items replaced = (40 + 20 + 50) = 110

New sum = (4700 + 210 – 110) = 4800

The correct mean = (4800/100)

⇒ 48

**∴ The required mean is 48**

questions.question: A hall is 18 m long and 12 m broad. If the sum of the areas of the floor and the ceiling is equal to the sum of the areas of the four walls, the volume (in m³) of the hall is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the hall = 18 m

The breadth of the hall = 12 m

the sum of the areas of the floor and the ceiling is equal to the sum of the areas of the four walls

**Formula used:**

Sum of the area of floor = Sum of the area of ceiling = Length × Breadth

Sum of the area of the four walls = 2 × Height(Length + Breadth)

The volume of the hall = Length × Breadth × Height 

**Calculation: **

Sum of area of floor = Sum of area of ceiling = (18 × 12) m²

⇒ 216 m²

Total area of floor and ceiling = (216 + 216) m²

⇒ 432 m²

Sum of area of 4 walls = 2 × H(18 + 12)

⇒ 60H

Now,

⇒ 60H = 432 m²

⇒ H = (432/60)

⇒ H = 36/5

Volume of the hall = (18 × 12 × 36/5)

⇒ (7776/5)

⇒ 1555.2 m³

**∴ The volume of the hall is 1555.2 m³**

questions.question: Two numbers are, respectively. 17% and 50% more than a third number. The ratio of the two numbers is:

**Calculation:**

⇒ (100x + 17x)

⇒ 117x

Second number is 50% more than the third number

questions.question: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the compound interest, when interest is compounded 6-monthly, and the simple interest on a sum of Rs.10,000 for 1(1)/(2) years at 10% p.a.?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 10,000

Time = 1(1)/(2) = 3/2 years

Rate = 10%

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)T

CI = (A – P)

SI = (P × R × T)/100

**Calculation:**

According to the question

CI for 6-monthly

P = Rs. 10,000

R = 10/2 = 5%

T = 1.5 years = 3 quarter

⇒ A = 10,000(1 + 5/100)³

⇒ 10,000(105/100)³

⇒ (10,000 × 21/20 × 21/20 × 21/20)

⇒ Rs. (92,610/8)

⇒ Rs. 11,576.25

CI = A – P

⇒ Rs. (11,576.25 – 10,000)

⇒ Rs. 1,576.25

Now,

SI = (10,000 × 10 × 3)/(2 × 100)

⇒ (10,000 × 30)/200

⇒ Rs. 1,500

Now,

Difference between CI and SI = Rs. (1,576.25 – 1,500)

⇒ Rs. 76.25

**∴ The required difference is Rs. 76.25**

questions.question: A sum (in Rs.) is distributed between A, B and C in the ratio 5 : 6 : 7. If B gives Rs.400 from his share to C, the ratio of the shares of A, B and C becomes 2 : 3 : 4. What is the sum of the shares (in Rs.) of A and c, in the beginning?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sum of the ratio of the A, B and C = 5x : 6x : 7x

B gives from his share to C = Rs. 400

The ratio of shares of A, B and C = 2 : 3 : 4

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

∵ 400 is given by B to C 

∴ Sum left with B = (6x - 400)

⇒ Sum left with C = (7x + 400)

Now,

New Ratio of the B and C = 3/4

⇒ (6x – 400)/(7x + 400) = 3/4

⇒ 24x – 1600 = 21x + 1200

⇒ (24x – 21x) = (1600 + 1200)

⇒ 3x = 2800

⇒ x = 2800/3

The sum of shares of A and C in the beginning = (5x + 7x) = 12x

⇒ (12 × 2800/3)

⇒ (4 × 2800)

⇒ Rs. 11,200

**∴ The required shares of A and C is Rs. 11,200**

questions.question: The cost price of 30 articles is the same as the selling price of x articles. If the profit is 25%, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The cost price of 30 articles is the same as the selling price of x articles

Profit = 25%

**Formula used:**

Profit = SP – CP

Profit% = Profit/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the CP of the each article be Rs. 1

CP of x article = Rs. x

And, SP of each article = Rs. 30

Profit = SP – CP

⇒ (30 – x)

Now,

Profit% = [(30 – x)/x × 100] = 25

⇒ 3000 – 100x = 25x

⇒ 3000 = 25x + 100x

⇒ 3000 = 125x

⇒ x = (3000/125)

⇒ x = 24

**∴ The value of the x is 24**

questions.question: A single discount equivalent to three simple discounts of 10%, 12% and 15% is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The three simple discounts = 10%, 12% and 15%

**Formula used:**

Equivalent discount = [100 – discounted value)/Initial value × 100]

**Calculation:**

Let the initial value be 100

According to the question

Discounted value = (100 – 10)% of (100 – 12)% of (100 – 15)% of 100

⇒ (90/100 × 88/100 × 85/100 × 100)

⇒ (9/10 × 22/25 × 85)

⇒ (9/5 × 11/5 × 17)

⇒ (1683/25)

⇒ 67.32

Equivalent discount = [100 – discounted value)/Initial value × 100]

⇒ [(100 – 67.32)/100 × 100]

⇒ (32.68 × 100)/100

⇒ 32.68%

**∴ A single discount equivalent to the three successive discounts is 32.68%**

questions.question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 10, 15 and 30 days, respectively. If B and C both assist A on every third day, then in how many days can the work be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by A = 10 days

Time taken by B = 15 days

Time taken by C = 30 days

B and C both assist on every third day

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

LCM of 10, 15 and 30 is 30

Efficiency of A = (30/10) = 3 units/days

Efficiency of B = (30/15) = 2 units/days

Efficiency of C = (30/30) = 1 units/days

Work done by A on first two days = (3 × 2) = 6

Work done by A, B and C on third day = (3 + 2 + 1) = 6 

Total work done by A, B and C in 3 days = (6 + 6) = 12 

Similarly,

Work done by A, B and C in next three days = 12 units

Total work done by A, B and C in 6 days = (12 + 12) = 24 unit

Remaining work = (30 – 24) units = 6 units

Number of days taken by A to complete the remaining work = (6/3) = 2 days

Total days = (3 + 3 + 2) = 8 days

**∴ The required time is 8 days**

questions.question: A train can travel 40% faster than a car. Both the train and the car start from point A at the same time and reach point B, which is 70 km away from point A, at the same time. On the way, however, the train lost about 15 minutes while stopping at stations. The speed of the car in km/h is:

A train can travel 40% faster than a car.

Both the train and the car start from point A at the same time and reach point B, which is 70 km away from point A

The train lost about 15 minutes while stopping at stations

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the car be x

Speed of the train = [x(1 + 40/100)]

⇒ (x × 140/100)

⇒ 140x/100

⇒ 1.4x

Time taken by car to cover 70 km

⇒ 70/x

Time taken by train to cover 70 km

⇒ 70/1.4x

According to the question

⇒ 70/x – 70/1.4x = 15/60

⇒ x = (70 – 50)/1/4

⇒ x = (20 × 4)

⇒ x = 80 km/h

**∴ The speed of the car is 80 km/h**

questions.question: If A and B can do a piece of work in 20 days, and A alone can do the same work in 30 days, then in how many days can B alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by A and B to do a piece of work = 20 days

Time taken by A alone to do the same work = 30 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

LCM of 20 and 30 is 60

Efficiency of A and B = (60/20) = 3 units/day

Efficiency of A = (60/30) = 2 units/day

Then,

Time taken by B alone to complete the same work = [(60/(3 – 2)]

⇒ 60/1

⇒ 60 days

**∴ The required time taken by B is 60 days**

questions.question: A field is in the form of a circle. The cost of fencing around it at Rs.11 per metre is Rs.2,420. What is the area (in m²) of the field? (Take pi = frac{{22}}{7})
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The cost of fencing around it at Rs. 11 per metre = Rs. 2,420

**Formula used:**

Perimeter of the circle = 2πr

Area of the circle = πr²

**Calculation:**

Cost of 1 m fencing = Rs. 11 per metre

Total length of the fencing = (2,420/11)

⇒ 220 m

Now,

Perimeter of the circle = 2πr

⇒ 2 × 22/7 × r = 220

⇒ 44r/7 = 220

⇒ r = (220 × 7)/44

⇒ r = 35 m

Now,

Area of the circle = πr²

⇒ (22/7 × 35 × 35) m²

⇒ (22 × 35 × 5) m²

⇒ 3850 m²

**∴ The area of the field is Rs. 3850 m²**

questions.question: A girl spend 76% of her income. If her income increase by 18% and her expenditure increases by 25%, then what is the percentage increase or decrease in her savings (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:

A girl spend her income = 76%

Her income increase = 18%

Her expenditure increases = 25%

Let the income of the woman be Rs. 100

Expenditure of woman =(76% of 100)

⇒ 76

Saving = (100 – 76) = 24

When income increased by 18%

New income of the woman = 100 + 18% of 100

⇒ (100 + 18/100 × 100) = 118

When expenditure increased by 25%

New expenditure of the woman = 76 + 25% of 76

⇒ (76 + 25/100 × 76)

⇒ (76 + 1/4 × 76)

⇒ (76 + 19)

⇒ 95

New saving = (118 – 95)

⇒ 23

Saving decreases = (24 – 23) = 1

Percentage decreases = (1/24 × 100)

⇒ 25/6

⇒ 4.166% ~ 4.2%

questions.question: The average weight of 6 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them weighing 55 kg. What might be the weight (in kg) of the new person?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of 6 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them weighing 55 kg

**Concept used:**

Weight of new person = Weight of the person being replaced + Total change in weight 

**Calculation:**

Weight of the person replaced = 55 kg

Total change in weight due to new person = 2.5 kg per person for 6 people

Total change in weight due to new person = (2.5 × 6) = 15 kg

Weight of the new person = (55 + 15) kg

⇒ 70 kg

**∴ Weight of the new person is 70 kg**
